analysis: Examined the three modified provider-swift files. (1) MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (head 1014-1686): the makeEventStream forwarder. GLM withholding of a JSON answer (glmAnswer) is applied in emit() and the validated answer is yielded only after validatedAnswer(finishReason:). Every error path calls releaseBox.fire() before finish(throwing:), so there is no plaintext leak on failure (T-008 is not regressed). Native-media terminal-drain, cancellation and lease handling keep upstream cancellation and release on each exit, so there is no new availability or resource leak (T-010). The GLM media guard (patch lines ~509-519) rejects JSON response_format or forced tools with media before inference, which is fail-closed. The non-native fallback path is unchanged. Inference content is not logged. The telemetry emits only constant strings and a mode value. (2) MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineError.swift: adds an unsupportedOutputControl case parsed by prefix before the generic substring checks. It sits ahead of the 'queue full'/'token_budget_exhausted' matching, so a prefixed message cannot be misclassified. The message is echoed back only as the error text; it is produced by the provider's own translation layer, so no new disclosure is evident. The prefix constant EngineV2Translation.unsupportedOutputControlPrefix and the 400 status mapping are outside the supplied evidence. (3) FlintResponseFormat.swift removes requireExplicitTypes. Untyped schema leaves are now compiled by the shared compiler, which infers string for untyped leaves per the removed comment. This may narrow the constraint relative to accept-anything, but validate() still checks output against the compiled schema. The risk is functional or correctness only, with no confidentiality, authorization or billing impact; the ToolConstraintSchemaCompiler behaviour is not visible here. No threat-model assets (keys, attestation, prefix cache) are touched. Remaining unverified: the status mapper handling of the new error case and the compiler's untyped-leaf behaviour.
